core_obligations: Reduce to a computation at each object: for an object V of the category, the preceding analysis of the integral Cech complex shows that Z_{U, bullet}(V) is isomorphic as a complex to a direct sum of complexes homotopic to Z placed in degree zero, hence Z_{U, bullet}(V) tensor_Z O(V) is isomorphic to a direct sum of complexes homotopic to O(V) placed in degree zero and is exact in positive degrees (proof lines 1173-1180).

Supply an alternative route: one may instead invoke the flat-resolution statement of the modules chapter, which applies because the presheaves Z_{U, i} are flat and the same analysis shows H_0(Z_{U, bullet}) is a flat presheaf as well (proof lines 1181-1185).

Conclude for the complex of presheaves: since exactness is tested at every object, the displayed chain complex Z_{U, bullet} tensor_Z O is exact in positive degrees, which is the assertion of the statement whose slogan is that the integral Cech complex is a flat resolution of the constant presheaf of integers (proof lines 1172-1186).
proof_roadmap: Evaluate at an object and use the known shape of the integral Cech complex to reduce to complexes homotopic to Z in degree zero (proof lines 1173-1177).
Tensor with the ring of sections and read off exactness in positive degrees (proof lines 1178-1180).
Optionally re-derive the same conclusion from flatness of the terms and of H_0 by the flat-resolution criterion (proof lines 1181-1185).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that tensoring the integral Cech chain complex of a family over a category with an arbitrary presheaf of rings yields a complex that is still exact in positive degrees, a statement whose slogan is that the integral Cech complex is a flat resolution of the constant presheaf of integers (statement lines 1151-1169). The proof is short because it reuses the structure of the integral complex: at each object the complex splits as a direct sum of complexes homotopic to Z in degree zero, and tensoring preserves that shape, the homotopy being preserved by an additive functor (proof lines 1173-1180). The author also records a second route through flatness of the terms and of H_0 (proof lines 1181-1185). The claim is H2: one reduction plus one preservation observation, with no new construction.
